requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM customer_case WHERE case_id = 181 AND priority = 'critical' AND escalation = 1 AND escalation_reason = 'impact'
assumptions: 'the open ticket regarding the PA-3220 V8' is case 181: of Stark Industries' three open cases on product 140 (181, 184, 200) it is the only one not already in_progress, and the request asks to move the ticket to in progress
policy: an escalation records escalation = 1 and captures escalation_reason; the acting user (4, a manager) may escalate and override priority
escalation_reason = impact kept from the benchmark check; not fixed by request or policy (customer_request and urgency would also fit the request, and nothing in it contradicts impact)

both passes relaxed escalation_reason to IS NOT NULL as undecidable; impact kept instead, since the benchmark's cell stands where neither the request nor the policy contradicts it, so the check is kept

requirements.text: the unit ending in 8853 at our London HQ is bricked. Mark it for repair.
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM installed_product WHERE installed_product_id = 42 AND status = 'repair'
assumptions: 'ending in 8853 at our London HQ' matches only installed product 42 (serial P140-898548-8853, account 8, location 817 'Stark Industries Hq - London', in_use on the seed)

requirements.text: Register a replacement unit I just bought (Serial: RMA-STARK-001) at the same spot.
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM installed_product WHERE installed_product_id = 301 AND account_id = 8 AND product_id = 140 AND location_id = 817 AND serial_number = 'RMA-STARK-001' AND status = 'in_use'
assumptions: id assumed next in sequence (301 after 300); the only installed product the task creates
a replacement for the swapped-out PA-3220 V8 is the same product, 140; 'the same spot' is location 817, where unit 42 sits
status in_use because the unit replaces one in service and the policy requires installed products attached to cases to be in_use (in_stock rejected); warranty_end not stated, not tested

requirements.text: Swap the hardware (the ticket regarding the PA-3220 V8 then refers to the replacement unit)
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM customer_case WHERE case_id = 181 AND installed_product_id = 301 AND product_id = 140
assumptions: the request does not say to re-point the ticket in so many words; read from 'Swap the hardware' on the open ticket plus the policy's rule that items in repair status are not attached to cases and installed products must be in_use, so case 181 (new) moves from unit 42 to the only in_use PA-3220 V8 unit, 301; kept from the benchmark check

requirements.text: Assign the ticket to Installed Base Support
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM customer_case WHERE case_id = 181 AND assignment_group_id = 10
assumptions: 'Installed Base Support' is the active support group of exactly that name (group 10); the _2/_3/_4 namesakes (30, 50 inactive, 70) are not it

requirements.text: update the status to in progress
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM customer_case WHERE case_id = 181 AND state = 'in_progress'
assumptions: new -> in_progress is a valid transition under the policy's lifecycle

requirements.text: update the status to in progress (policy: when a new case moves to work in progress the appropriate SLA is aligned to it; the ticket is now critical)
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM case_sla WHERE case_id = 181 AND sla_def_id = 6 AND stage = 'in_progress' AND has_breached = 0
assumptions: for a critical case the resolution definition is 6 (SLA Resolution - Critical), the only active one; case 181 carries only the high-priority SLAs 11 and 7 (rows 361, 362) on the seed, which the request does not mention and which are not tested

selected by natural key (case 181, definition 6), not by case_sla_id 2465: the policy's 'appropriate SLA' may also bring in the critical response SLA (definition 1), so how many case_sla rows the task creates is not fixed and the sequence position is undecidable
has_breached = 0 kept from the benchmark check: a freshly started SLA has not breached

requirements.text: Send me a confirmation email at marc.henry@stark-industries.com.
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM notification WHERE notification_id = 734 AND case_id = 181 AND email = 'marc.henry@stark-industries.com' AND type = 'update' AND status = 'success'
assumptions: id assumed next in sequence (734 after 733); the only notification the task creates
type update read from 'confirmation' of the changes made to the ticket (the enumeration has no confirmation value; other, the catch-all, rejected); kept from the benchmark check
status success is what a sent email means
the email is the one the request gives (Marc Henry, contact 10, the account's primary contact), not the acting user's

requirements.text: an open ticket regarding the Palo Alto PA-3220 V8 (boundary: the account's other PA-3220 V8 tickets stay as they are)
requirements.selector: account_id = 8 AND product_id = 140 AND case_id <> 181 AND (priority = 'critical' OR escalation = 1 OR assignment_group_id = 10)
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM customer_case WHERE account_id = 8 AND product_id = 140 AND case_id <> 181 AND (priority = 'critical' OR escalation = 1 OR assignment_group_id = 10)
assumptions: boundary of the ticket selector: cases 184 and 200 are also open on product 140 for account 8 (both in_progress, moderate) and must not be escalated, raised to critical or assigned to group 10; the selector also covers the account's other tickets on the product (189 resolved, 193 closed, 194 canceled)

disagreement: selector: A account_id = 8 AND product_id = 140 AND case_id <> 181 AND (priority = 'critical' OR escalation = 1 OR assignment_group_id = 10), B case_id IN (184, 200) AND priority = 'critical'; chose A's because it finds the rows by the description a loose reading would use and also catches the escalation flag and the assignment (both 0 on the seed)

disagreement: selector: A serial_number LIKE '%8853%' AND installed_product_id <> 42 AND status = 'repair', B installed_product_id IN (2, 108) AND status = 'repair'; the same two rows; chose A's because it finds them by the description a loose reading would use

critical_resolution_sla_linkage.evidence: the anchor case_sla_id = 2465 presumes the resolution SLA is the only case_sla row the task creates; the policy's 'appropriate SLA' may also add the critical response SLA (definition 1), so the row is selected by case 181 and definition 6 instead, with the same cells

notes:
Merged from two passes that agree on the eight shared requirements (escalation of case 181 to critical, unit 42 to repair, unit 301 registered at location 817, case 181 re-pointed to 301, group 10, state in_progress, the critical resolution SLA by natural key, notification 734) and on all eight dispositions. disagreement: the other-tickets stay's selector: A by description (account 8, product 140, not 181, with any of critical, escalated or group 10), B case_id IN (184, 200) AND priority = 'critical'; kept A's as the tighter predicate that finds the rows by description (logged in the requirement). disagreement: the other-serials stay's selector: A serial_number LIKE '%8853%' AND installed_product_id <> 42 AND status = 'repair', B installed_product_id IN (2, 108) AND status = 'repair'; the same rows; kept A's by description (logged in the requirement). Both passes relaxed escalation_reason = 'impact' to IS NOT NULL and marked the escalation check repaired; impact is kept and the check is kept, since the benchmark's cell stands where neither the request nor the policy fixes or contradicts it. The ticket is case 181 because 'update the status to in progress' rules out 184 and 200, which are already in_progress. This policy variant (sha1 60026242) has no mandatory-interaction rule and no explicit SLA-linking section; the SLA requirement rests on 'when new case moves to work in progress appropriate SLA should be aligned to it', and only the resolution SLA the benchmark tests is required (a critical response SLA may also be linked; neither pass tests it either way, and nothing in the request plainly asks for it). Least certain: the re-pointing of the ticket to unit 301, which both passes read from 'Swap the hardware' plus the policy's in_use rule rather than from an explicit sentence; the benchmark's check is the prior. The acting user is Joanne Simpson (user 4, manager), relaying a request in the voice of Stark Industries' Ops Lead Marc Henry (contact 10); the email is the request's, so no benchmark check rests on the acting user. No case-notes table exists for the escalation justification; completing or cancelling the old high-priority SLAs 361 and 362 is required by neither the request nor the policy.
revised: the escalation_reason assumption and note now state the reason for keeping impact directly.
